intro: New York's written test has 20 questions. You must answer at least 14 correctly, including two of the four road sign questions.

notes: You must correctly answer at least 14 of 20 questions AND at least 2 of the 4 road sign questions.
Class D knowledge tests are offered in multiple languages, on touch screens or paper.

commonMistakes.text: Turning right on red in New York City. It's not allowed unless a sign permits it.
Getting 14 right but missing 3 of the 4 sign questions — that's still a fail. Learn sign colors and shapes.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Vision and Knowledge Tests

commonMistakes.text: Assuming work-zone fines only double when workers are present. They double even when workers aren't there.
Forgetting that a traffic officer's direction overrides signals, signs and markings.

faq.q: How many questions are on the New York permit test?
faq.a: The written test has 20 questions. You must answer at least 14 correctly, including at least two of the four road sign questions.

faq.q: Which chapters of the Driver's Manual should I study?
faq.a: The manual's practice quizzes cover the rules-of-the-road chapters (Chapters 4 through 11) and the Road Signs section.

faq.q: How many supervised practice hours do junior drivers need?
faq.a: Junior drivers must certify at least 50 hours of practice, including at least 15 hours after sunset, on form MV-262 at the road test.

faq.q: Are these the official NY DMV test questions?
faq.a: No. They are original practice questions written from the New York State Driver's Manual, and each links to the chapter it comes from.

questions.question: In New York, warning signs are normally:
options: Yellow and diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols
questions.correctAnswer: Yellow and diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs normally are yellow and diamond-shaped, with black letters or symbols. They tell you that you are approaching a hazardous location or a location with a special rule.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs

questions.question: Destination signs in New York are:
questions.explanation: Destination signs are green with white letters and show the direction and distance to locations.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs: Destination Signs

questions.question: Blue signs with white letters or symbols show:
options: The location of services such as rest areas, gas, and medical facilities
questions.correctAnswer: The location of services such as rest areas, gas, and medical facilities
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters or symbols and show the location of services such as rest areas, gas stations, camping and medical facilities.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs: Service Signs

questions.question: Orange signs with black letters or symbols indicate:
options: People are working on or near the roadway
questions.correctAnswer: People are working on or near the roadway
questions.explanation: Work area signs are orange with black letters or symbols. A work-area speed limit as low as 25 mph can be posted, and you must always obey flag persons.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs: Work Area Signs

questions.question: Regulation signs in New York are normally:
options: White rectangles with black letters or symbols
questions.correctAnswer: White rectangles with black letters or symbols
questions.explanation: Regulation signs normally are white rectangles with black letters or symbols, though some are different shapes and some use red letters or symbols.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs

questions.question: A regulation sign showing a red circle with a slash over a symbol means:
options: The action shown is not allowed, or certain vehicles are restricted
questions.correctAnswer: The action shown is not allowed, or certain vehicles are restricted
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash over a symbol indicates that an action, like a right turn, is not allowed or that some vehicles are restricted from the road.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs: Other Regulation Signs

questions.question: At a YIELD sign, you must:
options: Always come to a full stop
Stop only if a police officer is present
Slow down, prepare to stop, and come to a full stop if traffic conditions require it
questions.correctAnswer: Slow down, prepare to stop, and come to a full stop if traffic conditions require it
questions.explanation: At a YIELD sign, decrease speed and prepare to stop and yield to vehicles and pedestrians. You must come to a full stop if traffic conditions require it.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs: Yield Sign

questions.question: At a STOP sign with no stop line, where must you stop?
options: In the middle of the crosswalk
Past the crosswalk where you can see
questions.explanation: You must stop before the stop line if there is one. If not, stop before you enter the crosswalk. With neither, stop before entering the intersection at the point that gives you a view of traffic.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Signs: Stop Sign

questions.question: May you turn right on a steady red light in New York City?
options: Only where a sign permits it
questions.correctAnswer: Only where a sign permits it
questions.explanation: You are not allowed to turn on a red light in New York City unless a sign that permits it is posted.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Traffic Signals: Steady Red

questions.question: Outside New York City, when may you turn left on a steady red light?
options: When turning from a one-way road into another one-way road, after stopping and yielding
questions.correctAnswer: When turning from a one-way road into another one-way road, after stopping and yielding
questions.explanation: You can turn left at a steady red light when turning from a one-way road into another one-way road, after a full stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians — unless a sign, signal, or marking prohibits it.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Traffic Signals: Steady Red

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same as:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a STOP sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Traffic Signals: Flashing Red

questions.question: What does New York law require if the traffic lights at an intersection are out of service?
options: Proceed as if the light were green
Stop as you would for a stop sign, then follow right-of-way rules
Yield only to vehicles on the left
questions.correctAnswer: Stop as you would for a stop sign, then follow right-of-way rules
questions.explanation: State law requires that if traffic lights are out of service or not working correctly, you must stop as you would for a stop sign and then continue according to right-of-way rules.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Traffic Signals: Traffic Lights

questions.question: Above a lane, a steady yellow "X" means:
options: This lane is for left turns only
Do not drive in this lane
questions.explanation: Lane-use control lights: steady red X — do not drive in this lane; steady yellow X — move from this lane; flashing yellow X — left turns only; green arrow — you may use this lane.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Traffic Signals: Lane Use Control Lights

questions.question: Double solid lines separate two lanes. When may you cross them?
options: Whenever the road ahead is clear
Only to turn left into or out of the highway, such as at a driveway
questions.correctAnswer: Only to turn left into or out of the highway, such as at a driveway
questions.explanation: With double solid lines you cannot pass or change lanes. You may cross only to turn left to enter or leave the highway (e.g., a driveway or a U-turn).
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Pavement Markings

questions.question: What does an edge line that angles toward the center of the road indicate?
options: The shoulder may be used as a lane
questions.explanation: An edge line that angles toward the center of the road shows that the road is narrower ahead.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Pavement Markings: Edge and Lane Lines

questions.question: A diamond symbol painted in a lane indicates:
options: A reserved lane, such as for buses, HOVs, or bicycles
questions.correctAnswer: A reserved lane, such as for buses, HOVs, or bicycles
questions.explanation: The diamond symbol indicates reserved lanes for buses, high-occupancy vehicles, bicycles or other special vehicles.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Pavement Markings: Diamond Symbol

questions.question: A traffic officer signals you to drive through a red light. What should you do?
options: Wait for the light to turn green
questions.explanation: Directions given by traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals, or pavement markings. If an officer signals you to drive through a red light, you must do it.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 4: Traffic Control — Traffic Officers

questions.question: To pass New York's written test, how many questions must you answer correctly?
questions.explanation: To pass the written test for a Class D, M, DJ, MJ or E license, you must correctly answer at least 14 of the 20 questions.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Vision and Knowledge Tests

questions.question: Besides getting 14 of 20 correct, what else does the New York written test require?
options: Correctly answering two of the four road sign questions
Answering all road sign questions correctly
questions.correctAnswer: Correctly answering two of the four road sign questions
questions.explanation: You must correctly answer at least 14 of the 20 questions, and you must correctly answer two of the four questions about road signs.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Vision and Knowledge Tests

questions.question: What vision standard must you meet to pass New York's vision test?
options: 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses
questions.correctAnswer: 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses
questions.explanation: To pass the vision test, you must have 20/40 vision in at least one eye with or without corrective lenses.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Vision and Knowledge Tests

questions.question: With a New York learner permit, your supervising driver must be at least:
options: 21 years old and licensed for the vehicle you're driving
questions.correctAnswer: 21 years old and licensed for the vehicle you're driving
questions.explanation: When you practice, you must be supervised by a licensed driver who is at least 21, holds a license valid for the vehicle, and is seated in the front seat with you.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — The Learner Permit and Road Test

questions.question: Before your road test, the manual says you should have at least 50 hours of practice. How many of those should be after sunset?
questions.explanation: It is important to have at least 50 hours of practice, with at least 15 hours after sunset. Junior drivers must present form MV-262 certifying this.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Preparing for the Road Test

questions.question: How long must a junior learner permit be held before taking the road test?
questions.explanation: Your permit must be held in valid status for a minimum of six months in order to take the road test.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — For Junior Drivers with Permits

questions.question: With a junior learner permit in New York City (the 5 boroughs), when may you NOT drive?
questions.explanation: Under the regional restrictions for a junior permit in New York City, you must NOT drive between 9 PM and 5 AM.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Regional Restrictions for a Junior Permit

questions.question: If you hold a junior permit, who is the only passenger allowed in the front seat?
options: Any passenger wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: If you hold a junior permit, the only passenger allowed in the front seat is your supervising driver.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Driving with a Junior Learner Permit

questions.question: How soon must you notify New York DMV after changing your address?
questions.explanation: If you change your address you must notify DMV within 10 days.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Change of Address

questions.question: After becoming a New York resident, how long do you have to get a New York driver license?
questions.explanation: Drivers who have moved here must turn in their out-of-state license and get a New York license within 30 days of becoming a permanent resident.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Driver Licenses

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Junior Operator (Class DJ) license?
questions.explanation: The Junior Operator, Class DJ license has a minimum age of 16, with restrictions on where, when, and with whom you can drive.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Driver Licenses — Types of Licenses

questions.question: If no speed limit is posted in New York State (outside cities with lower limits), the maximum is:
questions.explanation: You must obey the speed limit. If no limit is posted, drive no more than 55 mph.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Speed

questions.question: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit in New York City?
questions.explanation: The speed limit is 25 mph in New York City unless another limit is posted.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Speed

questions.question: New York's manual recommends the two-second rule. In bad weather or when following large trucks, you should increase it to at least:
questions.explanation: Use the two-second rule for a good space cushion. In bad weather and when following large trucks, increase the count to at least three or four seconds.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Allow Yourself Space

questions.question: An aggressive driver is following you. What should you do?
options: Don't stop or leave your vehicle; drive to the nearest police station
questions.correctAnswer: Don't stop or leave your vehicle; drive to the nearest police station
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is following you, do not stop or leave your vehicle. Drive to the nearest police station.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Aggressive Drivers

questions.question: Approaching a roundabout, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Roundabouts follow the yield-at-entry rule: look to the left — traffic in the roundabout has the right-of-way. Enter when there is an adequate gap.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Roundabouts

questions.question: Modern roundabouts are designed to restrict the speed of all vehicles within them to:
questions.explanation: Roundabouts are designed so that the speed of all vehicles is restricted to 30 mph (50 km/h) or less within the roundabout.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Roundabouts

questions.question: In New York, a first offense for talking on a hand-held phone while driving can bring a fine of up to $200 and how many license points?
questions.explanation: Speaking into or listening to a hand-held mobile phone while driving is a traffic infraction. A first offense can mean a fine of up to $200 and five license points.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Using a Cellular or Mobile Telephone

questions.question: A junior or probationary driver is convicted of using a hand-held phone while driving for the first time. The penalty is:
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary and junior licenses who use a hand-held phone or text while driving receive a 120-day suspension for a first conviction.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Penalties for Texting, Electronic Device Use

questions.question: New York law requires tires to have at least how much tread?
questions.explanation: The law requires that your tires have at least 2/32nds of an inch of tread. It is also illegal to drive on tires with cuts down to the cords, bumps, or bulges.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Vehicle Condition

questions.question: How far should you sit from the air bag cover in the steering wheel?
options: At least 10 inches from the center of your chest
questions.correctAnswer: At least 10 inches from the center of your chest
questions.explanation: You should sit with at least 10 inches between the center of your chest and the cover of the air bag.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

questions.question: Under New York law, a child must ride rear-facing until at least what age (or the seat's limit)?
questions.explanation: A child under four must be in a federally approved child safety seat, and must ride rear-facing until two years old or until reaching the seat's highest weight or height limit.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

questions.question: Children between ages 4 and 7 must generally ride in:
options: The front seat with a lap belt
An appropriate child restraint such as a booster seat used with a lap and shoulder belt
questions.correctAnswer: An appropriate child restraint such as a booster seat used with a lap and shoulder belt
questions.explanation: A child between four and seven must be restrained in an appropriate federally approved child restraint system, commonly a booster seat used with a lap and shoulder belt.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

questions.question: A driver who fails to buckle up in New York can face a fine of up to:
questions.explanation: The driver must be properly restrained by a seat belt and can face a fine of up to $50 for failing to buckle up.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

questions.question: Speeding fines in New York work zones double:
options: Even when workers or work vehicles are not there
questions.correctAnswer: Even when workers or work vehicles are not there
questions.explanation: When you speed in work zones, ticket fines double, even when the workers or work vehicles are not there.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — How to Drive Safely in Work Zones

questions.question: To prevent drowsy driving on a long trip, how often does the manual suggest scheduling stops?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, schedule regular stops for every 100 miles or two hours, get enough sleep, and plan long trips with a companion.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — Drowsy and Fatigued Driving

questions.question: A flagger in a work zone signals you to stop. The flagger's direction:
options: Can be ignored if the light is green
Has the same authority as a sign, and you can be ticketed for disobeying it
questions.correctAnswer: Has the same authority as a sign, and you can be ticketed for disobeying it
questions.explanation: A flagger has the same authority as a sign, which means you can receive a ticket for disobeying their directions.
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 8: Defensive Driving — How to Drive Safely in Work Zones
